bug_semantics: Stored XSS in the CMS page editor: Admin CMS create/update persist locale html_content from the HTTP POST body with no server-side HTML sanitization. TinyMCE on the admin textarea is the only script filter (it wraps or drops <script> in the UI). An authenticated admin who intercepts PUT/POST /admin/cms/edit/{id} (or create) and writes raw JavaScript into en[html_content] / html_content stores the payload unchanged. PageRepository only rewrites '=>' to '=>'. The storefront then emits the stored HTML unescaped via {!! $page->html_content !!} in packages/Webkul/Shop/src/Resources/views/cms/page.blade.php, and the admin editor reloads it into TinyMCE, so the script runs in admin or shop origin.
flaw_origin: The missing server-side sanitize-on-write was first written when CMS pages landed. Commit b1285fa2433f58f7ea6d3eeee363876b8d471fe2 (2019-08-02, Prashant Singh) added packages/Webkul/CMS/src/Http/Controllers/Admin/PageController.php store()/update() that copied request content into storage with no purify, plus TinyMCE on the CMS textarea as the only filter. Same-day follow-up 9ca97aa594f44b0ee1e39fd2ed78c804d78013fd renamed the field to html_content and added unescaped storefront rendering. Later Admin file-move and request()->only refactors preserved the unsanitized persist through v2.3.9. Helper clean_content() (HTML Purifier) already existed by v2.3.8 for other TinyMCE fields but was not applied to CMS until 0a9059d5a7dc0def3f4cd1d2beaf48efc0d719b8.

reasoning: CVE-2026-21451 / GHSA-2mwc-h2mg-v6p8 is a real published stored-XSS (CWE-79), not withdrawn. The attack is TinyMCE-only script wrapping on the CMS editor, bypassed by rewriting html_content on the raw CMS POST; the backend stores the payload and the shop/admin renders it as HTML. The GHSA commit URL points at the review-attachment SVG sanitizer (f533b1cd), which does not touch CMS html_content; the matching fix is 0a9059d5, which applies the existing clean_content()/Purify helper on PageController store/update and is an ancestor of tag v2.3.10. git log -L on store() plus --follow file history traces the unsanitized persist to the first CMS commit b1285fa (2019-08-02). That commit's parent tree has no CMS package, so the vulnerable lines are absent immediately before it. Same-day html_content rename and later Admin/Vue request()->only rewrites are refactors of that persist, not a smaller first-write. The BIC commit object is a human Webkul author/committer with no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailers; AI is judged only from that object, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
